metadata.note: The Ithaca and Owego Railroad -- one of the earliest railroads in the United States, and Ithaca's first passenger rail connection. Incorporated Jan 28 1828, built 1833-1834, and completed by April 1834: horse-drawn cars on wooden rails topped with strap iron, carrying plaster, salt, and (in 4 of the train's 49 cars) passengers on the ~29-mile run to Owego, where it met the Susquehanna River corridor. The route's signature feature was South Hill: climbing out of the Ithaca valley along Six Mile Creek required a stationary-engine-powered inclined plane (1,733.5 ft long, rising 1 in 21) followed by a second, horse-powered plane. A steam locomotive was added in 1840, though the Owego run still took over 3 hours. The Cayuga and Susquehanna Railroad bought the line June 6 1843; by 1851 the inclined planes had been replaced by switchbacks and a long valley loop. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad leased it in 1855, running it thereafter as the 'DL&W Ithaca Branch' (see scranton_railroads.geojson for DL&W's separate east-west Hoboken-Buffalo main line, which this branch fed into at Owego). Passenger service was discontinued March 29 1942. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation (Ithaca-Caroline-Candor-Catatonk-Owego) following the railroad's own documented station list, straight-line segments between those stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps, and does not attempt to depict the inclined planes' exact alignment.
sources: https://www.vizettes.com/kt/rr/ithaca-railroads/more-rr-info.htm and https://nyrails.org/railroads/delaware-lackawanna-and-western-railroad/dlw-ithaca-branch/ (incorporated Jan 28 1828, built 1833-34, completed April 1834; horse-drawn, 4 of 49 cars carrying passengers; steam locomotive added 1840; station list Ithaca-Lower Switch-Upper Switch-Conover-Summit-Caroline-Wilseyville-Candor-Catatonk-Owego; South Hill inclined planes, first 1,733.5ft at 1-in-21 grade; Cayuga and Susquehanna purchase June 6 1843; planes replaced by switchbacks/loop by 1851)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ithaca_and_Owego_Railroad (DL&W leased the Cayuga and Susquehanna in 1855; passenger service discontinued March 29 1942)

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
